This initial body size necessitates intensive and sustained parental provisioning, as the nestlings are entirely dependent on their parents for thermoregulation and food delivery during the first week of life. The rapid growth trajectory that follows is fueled by a diet consisting primarily of arthropods, which the parents collect from surrounding grasslands and arable fields. Field observations indicate that the nestlings develop quickly, gaining mass at a steady rate as they transition from a downy, immobile state to a feathered, more active condition within the nest. The timing of hatching itself is often synchronized with peaks in local insect abundance, a strategy that maximizes the availability of prey for the growing brood.
